CSCA Mock Test

Full-length, timed CSCA mock exams that work like the real paper: 48 single-choice questions in 60 minutes, scored from 0 to 100. 10 mock exams each for Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry, with an explanation for every answer.

Ready for a full timed mock?

Full-length mocks require Full Access. Compare the current plan and price before signing up. Already have access? Choose a Mathematics, Physics or Chemistry mock in your Practice dashboard.

See plans and pricingTry free questions

How the mock tests match the real CSCA exam

Each CSCA.ai mock exam follows the format of the CSCA exam Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry papers. Use your mock results to find topic gaps and timing problems; a practice score cannot predict your official result.

48 single-choice questions, one correct option each

60 minutes, with a running timer

Scored from 0 to 100, every question worth the same

A full explanation for every question after you submit

Check your current exam notice for permitted equipment. The published Mathematics syllabus does not specify whether calculators are allowed.

Mock tests or practice questions?

Start with a free five-question test in Mathematics, Physics or Chemistry. It takes two minutes and does not require an account. Full Access includes the 48-question, 60-minute subject mocks when you are ready to practise exam pacing. Our 90-day CSCA study plan shows when to make that switch. For the organizer's sample PDFs and a way to review each timed attempt, read our mock-test practice guide. Keep track of recurring mistakes with the blank CSCA error log.

Prefer to practise on paper? Download our free nine-question CSCA practice worksheet (PDF) for Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry, with worked answers. It is original CSCA.ai practice material, not an official past paper or a full-length mock exam.

Try free five-question practiceCompare Free and Full Access

To take a full mock, create an account, get Full Access, then choose a subject mock exam in your Practice dashboard. Check the current price before paying.

Where can I find official CSCA sample questions?

The exam organizer publishes sample-question PDFs for Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry on its official website. They show example questions, not complete papers from previous sittings. Open the subject you need, check the current syllabus, then use a timed mock to practise a full 60-minute paper.

These links lead to the organizer's files. CSCA.ai's free questions and full mocks are independently written practice, not official samples or verified past papers.

CSCA mock test questions

Is there a free CSCA mock test?

The free test has five questions and a two-minute timer for each subject, with no sign-up. The 48-question, 60-minute mock exams are included in paid CSCA.ai Full Access. Try free practice first, then compare the plan before upgrading.

How accurate are CSCA.ai mock tests compared with the real exam?

They follow the published subject syllabus and 48-question, 60-minute format, but they are original practice questions. Future official questions and difficulty can differ. Use a mock score to find topics and timing to improve, not to predict your official score or admission result.

Are these official CSCA past papers?

No. CSCA.ai writes its own mock questions using the published syllabus and exam format. The exam authority publishes sample-question PDFs; these mocks are not official papers or verified copies of previous sittings.

How many CSCA mock tests are there?

10 full mock exams each for Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry, so 30 in total.

Is there a mock test for Professional Chinese?

Not yet. The Professional Chinese paper has 80 questions in 90 minutes. Chinese-taught applicants generally take it; fully English-taught scholarship applicants should confirm their requirement with their university because published guidance differs. Our mock tests cover Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry.

When should I start taking full mock tests?

Once you have worked through most topics, usually 3 to 4 weeks before your session. Take one mock a week at first, review every mistake, then move to two a week in the final fortnight.
